title: Bishop diagonals
objective: Move a bishop diagonally, then capture on a clear diagonal.

commentary_source.name: Uroschess original beginner lesson
commentary_source.attribution: Original practice position and teaching text; not a historical game

steps.explanation: A bishop moves diagonally, through squares of the same colour. It can travel several squares when the path is clear.
steps.detail: You can ask for a hint or an answer if you need one.
steps.coach_prompt: Take one step at a time.

question.prompt: Move the bishop from c1 to f4.
hints: Follow the sloping line up and right from the bishop.

tree.feedback: Yes. Your bishop followed a diagonal from c1 to f4.
That is a legal diagonal move. For this first step, continue along the diagonal to f4.

question.other_legal_move_text: That move is legal. Try the destination named in the question.

steps.explanation: The bishop has moved. Find a black pawn on one of its diagonals. Bishops cannot jump over pieces.
steps.detail: You can ask for a hint or an answer if you need one.
steps.coach_prompt: Look for a capture on your own.

question.prompt: Capture a black pawn with your bishop.
hints: Look along both diagonals from the bishop.
One capture is from f4 to c7.

tree.feedback: Yes. Your bishop followed a clear diagonal and captured the pawn on c7.
That is a legal diagonal move, but it stops before a pawn. Look for a capture.
Yes. Your bishop followed the other clear diagonal and captured the pawn on h6.

question.other_legal_move_text: That move is legal, but it does not make the capture in this exercise. Look for a capture with your bishop.

takeaway: Bishops move diagonally and stay on the same square colour. Their path must be clear.
